form_cues: Bench angle at 30-45 degrees for upper chest emphasis
Lower the dumbbells to your upper chest, not your lower
Press and squeeze at the top — full lockout
routine.sourceQuote: Incline press first — upper chest is lagging for most people, hit it when you're fresh

form_cues: Arch slightly and tuck your shoulder blades back and down
Bar path slightly diagonal — toward lower chest
Touch the bar to your chest on every rep
routine.sourceQuote: Flat bench now — this is our heavy compound for the day, load it up

form_cues: Cables set to chest height, slight forward lean
Imagine hugging a large tree with a slight bend in the elbows
Feel the stretch at the start and squeeze at center
routine.sourceQuote: Cable flys for the stretch — if your gym doesn't have cables, use dumbbells on a flat bench

form_cues: Hinge forward until torso is nearly parallel to the floor
Pull the bar into your lower abdomen — not your chest
Hold the squeeze for one count before lowering
routine.sourceQuote: Moving to back now — barbell rows, heavy, full range of motion every rep

form_cues: Slight lean back, pull the bar to your upper chest
Elbows drive down and back — think about bending the bar
Slow on the way up — resist the weight
routine.sourceQuote: Lat pulldowns — keep that slight lean and drive those elbows down

form_cues: Cable set above eye level, rope attachment
Pull to your face — external rotation at the end
Elbows high, not low
exercises.sourceQuote: Superset alert — face pulls right into rear delt flys, huge for shoulder health

form_cues: Hinge forward slightly, arms out to the sides
Think about trying to touch your elbows behind your back
Light weight — it's about feel, not load
exercises.sourceQuote: Straight into rear delt flys — go lighter than you think, this is corrective work

form_cues: Bar starts at chin height, press straight up
Lock out fully overhead — squeeze the glutes
Keep your ribcage down, don't hyperextend the lower back
routine.sourceQuote: Shoulders now — OHP is the king of pressing, same rules as bench: full ROM

form_cues: High bar or low bar — pick your preference and stay consistent
Brace before you unrack — 360 degrees of tension in your torso
Depth to at least parallel; below parallel if mobility allows
routine.sourceQuote: Leg day portion starts here — squats, back to loaded, this is the heaviest set of the session

form_cues: Feet high and wide on the platform for more glute/ham
Lower until knees are at 90 degrees, not further
Don't lock out completely — keep tension on the quads
routine.sourceQuote: Leg press after squats — more volume on the quads while the load is lower

form_cues: Bar or dumbbell variant — both work equally well here
Push your hips back as far as possible before bending the knees
Load the hamstrings like a spring — then drive through the hips
routine.sourceQuote: RDLs for the hamstrings — this is where most people leave gains on the table

form_cues: Lying or seated — seated gives better peak contraction
Curl all the way up, pause, slow descent
Don't let your hips rise off the pad
routine.sourceQuote: Leg curls — hamstrings are a two-joint muscle, so both RDLs and curls matter

form_cues: Full range of motion — heel all the way down, then up on the ball of foot
Pause at the top for a one-second contraction
Calves respond well to higher reps and slow tempo
routine.sourceQuote: Finishing with calf raises — four sets, full ROM, don't rush these
